steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the 'http' and 'fs' modules using require() statements.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import each module. You'll need these for creating a server and working with files.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two require() statements that import the 'http' and 'fs' modules.
successCriteria: The 'http' and 'fs' modules are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the core modules needed for building a server and handling files.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you import both 'http' and 'fs' modules using require().
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import both the 'http' and 'fs' modules using require() statements.

steps.title: Create server instance
steps.instruction: Create an HTTP server instance using the http module's createServer() method. Store it in a constant named 'server'.
steps.hint: Use the http module you imported to call createServer() and assign the result to a constant.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a server instance
const server = http.createServer();
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a constant named 'server' that holds the HTTP server instance created by http.createServer().
successCriteria: The server constant is declared and assigned the result of http.createServer().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created an HTTP server instance. This server will listen for incoming requests once we configure it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the http module's createServer() method and storing it in a constant named 'server'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create an HTTP server instance using the http module's createServer() method and store it in a constant named 'server'.

steps.title: Define server request handler
steps.instruction: Add a callback function as the first argument to createServer() that handles incoming HTTP requests and responses.
steps.hint: The callback function should take two parameters: request and response. You can use an arrow function or function declaration.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createServer() call now includes a callback function that will process all incoming HTTP requests.
successCriteria: A callback function with req and res parameters is passed to createServer().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the request handler function. This function will be called for every incoming HTTP request.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a complete function with both req and res parameters inside createServer().
steps.feedbackWrong: The server instance should include a callback function as the first argument to createServer(). Try adding (req, res) => {} inside the parentheses.

steps.title: Initialize presence tracking data
steps.instruction: Create a variable named 'activeUsers' and initialize it as an empty array to store active user information.
steps.hint: Use the 'const' keyword to declare the variable and set it equal to an empty array [].
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an empty array for storing items
const shoppingCart = [];
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a variable ready to store user presence data when users connect to your tracker.
successCriteria: The 'activeUsers' variable is declared and initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the data structure to track active users.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a variable named 'activeUsers' and set it to an empty array [].
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a variable to store active user information as an array.

steps.title: Set up request routing logic
steps.instruction: Inside the request handler, add conditional logic to check the request URL and send different responses for the root path '/' and the '/status' path.
steps.hint: Use an if-else statement with req.url to check the path. Send a simple text response for each route.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will respond with different messages for the '/' and '/status' routes.
successCriteria: The request handler contains conditional logic that checks req.url and sends appropriate responses for '/' and '/status'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've implemented the routing logic. The server can now handle different paths.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some routing logic, but it doesn't handle both '/' and '/status' paths correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The routing logic is missing or doesn't check req.url to handle different paths.

steps.title: Create user join endpoint
steps.instruction: Inside the request handler, add an if statement to handle POST requests to the '/join' path. In the if block, parse the request body to get the username, add it to the users array, and send a JSON response confirming the user joined.
steps.hint: Check if req.method is 'POST' and req.url is '/join'. Use req.on('data') to collect the body data, then JSON.parse it. Push the username to the users array and respond with a success message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now accept POST requests to '/join' with a JSON body containing a username, add that user to the users array, and respond with a JSON success message.
successCriteria: The request handler includes an if statement checking for POST method and '/join' URL, parses the request body, pushes the username to the users array, and sends a JSON response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the user join endpoint. The server can now accept new users via POST requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the endpoint, but make sure to handle the request body parsing and respond with JSON. Check if you're using req.on('data') and req.on('end') to collect the body data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The endpoint isn't fully implemented. Ensure you're checking for POST method and '/join' URL, parsing the request body to get the username, adding it to the users array, and sending a JSON response.

steps.title: Create user leave endpoint
steps.instruction: Add a route handler for POST requests to '/leave' that removes a user from the users array based on the username sent in the request body.
steps.hint: Inside the request handler callback, check if the request method is 'POST' and the URL is '/leave'. Parse the request body to get the username, then filter it out from the users array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will handle POST requests to '/leave' by removing the specified user from the online list.
successCriteria: A POST route for '/leave' is implemented that removes users from the users array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the leave endpoint to remove users from the online presence list.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to properly parse the request body and filter the users array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The leave endpoint isn't working correctly. Check the routing logic and the array filtering.

steps.title: Create status check endpoint
steps.instruction: Inside the server's request handler, add a route for GET requests to '/status' that returns the users array as JSON.
steps.hint: Check if the request method is 'GET' and the URL is '/status', then set the response header for JSON and send the users array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will respond to GET requests at '/status' with a JSON array of online users.
successCriteria: A GET route for '/status' is implemented that returns the users array as JSON with proper headers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The status endpoint is now ready to show all online users.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure to check both the method and URL, set the Content-Type header, and send the users array as JSON.
steps.feedbackWrong: The status endpoint is not implemented correctly. Review the routing logic and JSON response format.

steps.title: Add basic HTML interface
steps.instruction: Inside the request handler, add a route for GET requests to '/' that serves a basic HTML page using fs.readFile() to read an HTML file.
steps.hint: Check if req.method is 'GET' and req.url is '/', then use fs.readFile() to read a file like 'index.html' and send it as the response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now respond to GET requests to the root URL with an HTML page, providing a basic web interface for the presence tracker.
successCriteria: The request handler includes a conditional check for GET requests to '/' that uses fs.readFile() to serve an HTML file with proper error handling.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the HTML serving route. Users can now access a web interface for the tracker.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some routing logic, but make sure to check for both GET method and '/' URL, and use fs.readFile() to serve the HTML file.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route for serving HTML is missing or incorrect. Review how to handle GET requests and serve files with fs.readFile().

steps.title: Start the server
steps.instruction: Call the server.listen() method to start your server listening on port 3000.
steps.hint: Add server.listen(3000) at the end of your code, after the server is created and your request handler is defined.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your server will be ready to accept incoming HTTP connections on port 3000.
successCriteria: The server.listen(3000) method is called to start the server.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your server is now configured to listen for connections on port 3000.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you call the listen method on your server instance with the correct port number.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server is not started correctly. You need to call server.listen(3000) to begin accepting connections.
